You are running on Windows. Follow these rules strictly:

1. **Executable resolution**: When a CLI tool is not found, check for `.cmd`

2. **Path separators**: Use `\` in Windows file paths when constructing

3. **Line endings**: Be aware of CRLF vs LF. When writing files, use the
   existing convention in the project.

4. **Never auto-install software**: Do not run `winget install`, `scoop install`,
   `choco install`, or similar without explicit user confirmation. If a program
   is missing, tell the user and suggest the install command — wait for approval.

5. **Shell syntax — PowerShell only**: Your shell is PowerShell, NOT bash/sh.
   Even when a skill shows bash examples, you must adapt to PowerShell conventions:
   - Do NOT use `&&` to chain commands — use `;` or `if ($?) { ... }`.
   - Do NOT use `ls -la` — use `Get-ChildItem` or `ls` without Unix flags.
   - Do NOT use `head`, `tail`, `grep`, `wc` — use `Select-Object -First`,
     `Select-Object -Last`, `Select-String`, `Measure-Object`.
   - Do NOT use `cd dir && command` — use the `workdir` parameter instead.
   - Do NOT use Bash-style `\"` escapes inside PowerShell strings.
   - Wrap regex/search patterns in single quotes, especially `rg` /
     `Select-String` patterns containing `|`, `(`, `)`, `\`, or `$`.
   - Do not wrap ordinary bash-tool commands in `powershell -Command`;
     the tool already runs through the selected Windows shell.
   - If launching a nested `pwsh`/PowerShell is unavoidable, prefer
     `pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command '<script>'` so the parent
     PowerShell does not expand `$variables` before the child sees them.
   - Skill READMEs may show bash/sh syntax as examples; translate to PowerShell
     or invoke via `bash -c "..."` (only if Git Bash is confirmed working).

6. **bash ≠ Git Bash on many Windows machines**: `bash.exe` on PATH may resolve
   to the WSL launcher (`WindowsApps\bash.exe`) instead of Git Bash. If `bash`
   produces garbled/UTF-16 output or WSL prompts ("install a distribution"),
   do NOT retry — switch strategy immediately:
   - For Node.js scripts: call `node script.cjs` directly.
   - For Python scripts: call `python script.py` directly.
   - If Git Bash is specifically needed, locate it via:
     `& "C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe" script.sh`

7. **PowerShell fail-fast**: For multi-statement scripts, start with
   `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'`. For native programs where non-zero
   exit codes must fail the script, set `$PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true`
   when available, or check `$LASTEXITCODE` explicitly.

8. **Error recovery — max 2 retries**: When a command fails, do NOT retry the
   same approach more than twice. After 2 failures with the same tool/syntax,
   you MUST switch to an alternative approach (different tool, different syntax,
   or skip the step). Burning 5+ turns on the same error wastes tokens and the

> ## Documentation Index > Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://platform.minimax.io/docs/llms.txt > Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further. # Hermes Agent > Use the latest MiniMax M-series models in Hermes Agent for autonomous AI-powered development.
[**Hermes Agent**](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent) is an open-source self-improving AI agent framework by Nous Research.
## Prerequisites * A MiniMax [Subscription Key](https://platform.minimax.io/user-center/payment/token-plan) with Token Plan or Credits access * A computer with terminal access (macOS, Linux, or Windows with WSL2) *** ## Install Hermes Agent [Hermes Agent](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent) is an open-source, self-improving AI agent built by [Nous Research](https://nousresearch.com). It features persistent cross-session memory, a built-in learning loop, 40+ integrated tools, and multi-platform access (CLI, Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp). Run the one-line installer in your terminal: ```bash theme={null} curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/main/scripts/install.sh | bash ``` Verify the installation: ```bash theme={null} hermes doctor ``` For more information, refer to the [Hermes Agent documentation](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/). ## Configure MiniMax Token Plan When using the one-click setup wizard, you can skip the manual installation above and run: ```bash theme={null} npx -y mmx-cli@latest agent setup ``` Select **Hermes Agent**. If it is missing, keep Hermes Agent selected in the second multi-select. The wizard runs the official installer's non-interactive core CLI stages, skips optional flows such as `setup` and `gateway`, and checks `hermes --version`. It then updates `~/.hermes/config.yaml` and `~/.hermes/.env`. See [One-click setup wizard](/docs/token-plan/agent-setup) for command options and backup behavior. Hermes Agent has built-in support for MiniMax as a provider. Run the model selector: ```bash theme={null} hermes model ``` 1. Select **"MiniMax (global endpoint)"** from the provider list. 2. When prompted, enter your **Subscription Key** obtained from the [MiniMax Token Plan page](https://platform.minimax.io/user-center/payment/token-plan). 3. Select **MiniMax-M3** as the model. Don't have resources yet? View your Subscription Key on the [Token Plan page](https://platform.minimax.io/user-center/payment/token-plan), then buy a Token Plan subscription or Credits, or use resources assigned by your Team. Subscription Keys are different from pay-as-you-go API Keys. ## Start Using Hermes Agent Run `hermes` to start talking with Hermes Agent powered by the latest MiniMax M-series models. Hermes Agent's persistent memory and self-improving skills system means it gets better the more you use it — your coding patterns, project context, and preferences are remembered across sessions automatically. ## Toggle thinking Toggle thinking at runtime with `/reasoning`: `none` turns it off, any other level (minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh) turns it on.

## The full pricing map (verified just now)

MiniMax has **two top-level categories**. That's it. Nothing hidden.

### 1. Subscription Plans (monthly, fixed quota)

| Plan | Price | What it covers |

   - Plus: $22/mo
   - Max: $55/mo
   - Ultra: $132/mo
   - Credits: $5 / $25 / $100 packs

These are TWO different products. MiniMax Design is for creators using the desktop app. Token Plan is for developers using the API in tools.

The answer is: YES, MiniMax Design ($10 starter) is a SEPARATE product from Token Plan ($22+). They're not the same.

The user wanted to know:
- Is the $10 plan an add-on to the $22 plan? NO — they're separate products.
- Where does Design fit? MiniMax Design is the creative studio desktop app.
- Which one do they need for Hermes Agent?

For Hermes Agent (programming, agentic CLI tool), the user needs:
- **Token Plan** ($22/mo Plus minimum) OR pay-as-you-go API OR Credits
